title: When Stored Evidence Stops Being Usable: Scale-Conditioned Evaluation of Agent Memory
claim: Growing irrelevant context, with evidence held fixed, raises interaction burden and pushes systems past their budget, so reliability breaks down at some scale.
layout: 3 colored panels left-to-right, causal chain, small mini-plots inset in last panel
description: Three tinted panels run left to right: blue (a), teal (b), orange (c). Panel (a) shows grids of squares labeled S0 to S4. Teal squares are fixed relevant evidence, and gray squares are irrelevant memory that grows with each grid. A brace marks the target question, and a color-graded arrow shows scale increasing. Green and orange arrows lead from the small and large grids into panel (b). Panel (b) compares a small-memory case, where a robot agent retrieves in one simple pass, with a large-memory case. In the large case the agent runs query-reformulation loops, inspects near-matches and distractors, and verifies, producing a long stack of retrieval calls. Panel (c) shows a vertical budget-limit bar labeled B. A green path ends in a success check mark. A tangled orange scribble ends in a failure cross. Three small line plots at the bottom show Pass@B falling, tail retrieval cost rising, and stronger versus weaker models.
caption: Overview of memory at scale. (a) Evidence-preserving scaling: task-relevant evidence is held fixed while irrelevant accessible memory grows. (b) Interaction burden: larger memories can trigger long-tail retrieve--verify loops (more agent-issued memory calls). (c) Reliability and usable-scale boundary: under a fixed retrieval budget, interaction burden and within-budget errors translate into failures, shifting the scale where reliability first falls below the target across agent--memory systems.
abstract: Memory-agent evaluations report fixed-snapshot accuracy or retrieval quality, but these scores do not show whether evidence remains usable as irrelevant sessions (sessions not annotated as task-relevant evidence for the query) accumulate. We present a scale-conditioned evaluation protocol for agent memory under evidence-preserving growth: for each query, task evidence is held fixed while irrelevant sessions are added. The protocol logs agent-memory trajectories and reports four diagnostics: budget-compliant reliability, tail memory-call burden, failure-regime decomposition, and the usable-scale boundary where reliability falls below the target. Applied to LongMemEval and LoCoMo across flat, planar, and hierarchical memory interfaces, the protocol shows reliability loss is not a single phenomenon. On LongMemEval, HippoRAG stays within the two-call budget but loses 16-20 percentage points in budget-compliant reliability as irrelevant sessions are added; LiCoMemory's observed failures depend strongly on the agent, with Qwen3-8B exceeding the budget while Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-235B remain reliable in the tested range. The result supports a framework for making scalable-memory claims conditional on agent, interface, scale range, and interaction budget. Code and evaluation artifacts: https://github.com/AndyLu666/memory-at-scale
